items.title: Robot Talk Episode 172 – Robots that learn like children, with Leticia Mara Berto

Her research takes inspiration from child development to develop cognitive abilities in robots. She is particularly interested in building autonomous robots by designing cognitive architectures, with an emphasis on intrinsic motivation, learning, and decision-making. items.title: FCC should focus on robot security, not country of origin
items.summary: The Go2 quadruped robot from Unitree, a prominent Chinese robot developer. | Source: Unitree The FCC is right to treat connected robots as a security issue . Its recent action restricting foreign-produced advanced robotic devices reflects a real risk. These machines carry cameras and sensors, transmit data, take remote software updates, and make their own decisions inside factories, warehouses, stores, and airports. But where a robot was assembled tells you little about who controls it once it's deployed. A robot built entirely in the United States, with unsigned updates and open remote access, is a bigger risk than one built overseas with secure software. The real security boundary is the code, the data, and whoever can change them, not the chassis. The FCC has already recognized this.
